newsitem.title: CHINA: China says S.Africa diplomatic switch to aid trade.
newsitem.headline: China says S.Africa diplomatic switch to aid trade.

text.p: South Africa's plan to forge diplomatic ties with China would boost trade and economic cooperation, an official newspaper said on Sunday.
The Business News quoted a leading Chinese specialist on South African trade issues as saying that Pretoria's plan to end formal ties with Taiwan would benefit South African companies.
South African President Nelson Mandela said late last month that Pretoria would cut diplomatic ties with Taiwan and establish full diplomatic relations with China by the end of 1997.

"If such words are carried out and diplomatic ties are established between the two sides, it is certain that Sino-South African trade and cooperation will gain impetus," the newspaper quoted Yang Lihua, director of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Centre for South African Studies, as saying.

China and Taiwan have been divided since the end of a civil war in 1949. Beijing views Taiwan as a rebel province that is not entitled to diplomatic ties with other states, and has tried to isolate the island politically.
Yang was quoted as saying that enterprises of the two countries had faced restrictions without full diplomatic links.
China would continue to import iron ore, automobile components, mineral exploration equipment, paper and wool from South Africa, Yang said.

She also said she saw new opportunities for South African companies in China's mining, energy and manufacturing sectors. Chinese companies could take advantage of South Africa's policy of encouraging labour-intensive investment and make use of the relatively good legal system in that country, she added.
Chinese manufactured goods such as electrical appliances and light industrial products had good prospects in South Africa, the newspaper quoted her as saying.
The paper quoted Chinese customs statistics as showing two-way trade at $1.3 billion last year compared with $900 million in 1994.
